knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A single case keeps the standard frequency for the area, but the method is raised to detergent plus disinfectant on most elements of the isolated room. Only an outbreak changes the whole area.
Raising a band is allowed where patients are at increased risk, but any change is agreed with clinical management and infection control. Lowering a band needs a major shift in case mix or service.
The standard says an outbreak temporarily upgrades any functional area to the top band, and it stays that way until the coordinators lower the outbreak status.

practicalCriteria: Assessor asks the learner to name the band of three areas on the facility map, with a pass where all three are correct
Learner names the person to consult before a change, with the correct role title
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Knowledge-check result (this result does not verify practical competence)
Assessor note of the map exercise
stopWorkCriteria: No current site schedule is available
An outbreak is reported and the new frequency is used before the coordinator approves it
